title: How fast did news travel? Lincoln, Custer, the Titanic and Pearl Harbor in America's newspapers
excerpt: I followed four great stories through 13,233 digitised issues of 936 American newspapers. A daily printed Lincoln's death the next morning, just as fast as the Titanic or Pearl Harbor. What held news back was the weekly press day.
seo_description: How many days did Lincoln's death, Custer, the Titanic and Pearl Harbor take to reach 936 American newspapers? Mapped day by day.
header_alt: Title card reading 'How fast did news travel?' on parchment above four small maps of the United States for Lincoln 1865, Little Bighorn 1876, Titanic 1912 and Pearl Harbor 1941, each covered in dots coloured from dark red for the next day to blue for three weeks or more.
